name: Woolly Bugger
recipe: Non-toxic wire to cover hook shank
Black or brown very webby rooster hackle

steps.text: Wrap bare hook shank with non-toxic wire and cover with a thread base.
Tie in a full marabou feather as a tail at a point above the hook barb. Lash the butt ends of marabou to the hook shank and return thread to the tail.
Tie in, in order, the wire ribbing, hackle feather (mounted by its tip), and chenille.
Wrap the chenille in touching turns to behind the hook eye. Tie off and trim the waste.
Wind the hacking forward in even, open turns to behind the hook eye. Tie off and trim the waste.
Counter wrap the wire through the hackle, wiggling the wire side to side to avoid binding down hackle barbs. Tie off, trim waste, and whip finish.

name: Tan Scud
recipe: 1/8" Mylar strip or latex scud back

steps.text: Wrap the bare hook shank with nontoxic wire and cover with a smooth base of thread.
Tie in the copper wire.
Tie in the strip of Mylar.
Spin dubbing thickly onto thread and wrap a rough shaggy body, leaving ~1.5-2 hook eye diameters of space behind the eye.
Pull the shellback over the body and tie off behind the eye. Wrap wire rib in an open spiral, tie off behind the eye, and whip finish.
Tease out dubbing fibers by brushing the sides and bottom with Velcro. The finished fly should be very shaggy.

name: Partridge & Orange
recipe: Hungarian partridge, tied sparsely as a collar

steps.text: Wrap a thread base over the thorax. Position the thread ~1.5 hook eye diameters behind the eye.
Remove the barbs from one side of the hackle stem. Tie in the hackle feather by its tip with bare stem laying against the hook shank. Trim waste.
Bind the floss to the hook shank and trim waste. Return the thread to the thorax.
Wrap a smooth and tapered floss body. Tie off the floss and trim waste.
Dub a bulbous thorax of hare's mask fur just behind the hackle tie-in point.
Wrap ~2 turns of hackle forward toward the hook eye. Tie off, trim waste, and whip finish.

name: Pass Lake
recipe: Peacock herl, 4-5 strands twisted with a piece of tying thread for reinforcement

steps.text: Wrap a thread base on the rear ~2/3 of hook shank and tie in the tail. The tail length should equal that of the hook shank.
Twist 4-5 strands of peacock herl with a piece of thread to make a rope. Wrap herl forward in touching turns to ~1/3 of hook shank behind the eye.
Stack a bundle of calf tail and tie it in with the tips extending over the hook bend to a point about mid-way along the tail.
Tie in the hen feather by its tip with the shiny side facing toward the hook eye.
Fold and preen the feather barbs backwards. Create a soft hackle collar by wrapping ~4 adjacent turns of hackle toward the hook eye.
Wrap a neat but pronounced head, whip finish, and apply head cement.
Insert the hook point into the smaller hole of a counter-drilled bead. Position the bead behind the hook eye.
Attach the tying thread behind the hook eye
Wrap a thread base in touching turns down hook the shank and partially around the bend. Tie in the ribbing wire.
Wrap the tying thread in touching turns up the hook shank to just behind the bead. The body should be smooth and uniformly black.
Wrap the ribbing wire in uniformly spaced spirals up the hook shank to just behind the bead. Tie off the wire and trim the waste end.
Build a neat thread head behind the bead. The thread head should secure the bead tightly against the hook eye. Whip finish and trim the thread.

name: X-Caddis
recipe: Ginger Z-lon (sparkly nylon) fibers, length equal to hook shank
Dry fly dubbing, color to match natural
Light or dark natural elk or deer hair, length to hook bend

steps.text: Wrap a smooth thread base from behind the eye to above the hook barb.
Position thread at ~1/3 shank length behind the hook eye and tie in the tailing material. Trim the waste ends.
Lash the tail fibers to the hook shank, finishing above the hook barb. Trim the length of the tail to equal the length of the hook shank.
Spin dubbing on thread and dub a body with a reverse taper (abdomen larger than thorax). Leave ~2 eye diameters of space behind the eye.
Clean, stack, and tie in a bundle of deer or elk hair, length reaching to hook bend. Keep all hair fibers atop the hook shank.
Gather the butt ends of the hair, lift them above the hook eye, and whip finish under the bundle. Trim the hair to form a prominent head.

name: BWO Sparkle Dun
recipe: Olive dry fly dubbing (Superfine, beaver, muskrat, etc.)

steps.text: Wrap a thread base. Stack a bundle of hair and tie in at ~1/3 shank length behind eye with tips pointing forward. Wing length equals hook shank length.
Trim hair at ~45° angle and bind the butt ends with thread. Pull wings upright and make a tight "wedge" of thread in front of the wing.
Tie in the tail and lash the fibers to the hook shank, ending at the base of wing butts. Trim the length of the tail to equal the hook shank.
Return the thread to the tail. Spin dubbing on thread and dub a thin, smooth, tapered abdomen up to the wing.
Apply more dubbing and dub in front of and behind the wing in a "figure-8". Dub a tapered thorax ending just behind the hook eye.
Tie off, whip finish, and apply head cement. Use your fingers to spread the wing hairs into a 180° arc around the top half of the fly.

name: Rusty Spinner
recipe: Microfibetts; tan, cream, gray, or brown; split widely; 1 or 2 fibers on each side

steps.text: Wrap a smooth thread base and tie in 2-4 microfibetts as a tail. Tail length should be ~1.5 - 2 times the length of the hook shank.
Divide the microfibetts into two widely split tails by placing figure-8 wraps around the base of the tail. Each side should consist of 1 or 2 fibers.
Bring the thread to ~1/4 of the shank behind the eye. Tie in a piece of white poly yarn parallel to hook shank with a couple of loose wraps.
Rotate the poly yarn perpendicular to the hook shank and tie it down firmly with figure-8 wraps.
Return the tying thread to the tail. Spin dubbing tightly onto the thread and wrap a thin and slightly tapered abdomen.
Dub the thread again and wrap a pronounced thorax. Whip finish behind the eye and trim the wings to a length slightly shorter than the hook shank.

name: Pink Squirrel
recipe: Heavy wire curved hook, #10 with a 1/8" gold bead
Hare's mask fur mixed with ice dubbing

steps.text: Thread the bead onto the hook (point goes into smaller hole). Add 5-6 wraps of wire for weight. Push the wire firmly up against the bead.
Cover the wire and hook shank with a thread base. Tie in the tail of Crystal Flash (6 strands total) and the wire ribbing.
Spin abdomen dubbing thickly onto thread and wrap a rough shaggy body to ~1/3 of the hook shank behind the eye.
Wind the wire ribbing through the abdomen in an open spiral. Tie off the wire and trim the waste.
Spin thorax dubbing thickly onto thread and dub a pronounced thorax. The pattern inventor, John Bethke, ties the thorax of Coral Pink chenille.
Whip finish behind the bead and apply head cement.

name: Gold-Ribbed Hare's Ear
recipe: Long hair fibers of a hare's mask

steps.text: Wrap wire weight on a bare hook shank. Attach thread and tie in the tail hair, underfur removed. Tail length equals ~1/2 of the hook shank.
Cover the wire with thread. Return thread to the rear and tie in the gold tinsel. Spin dubbing fur roughly onto thread.
Wrap dubbing to a point ~1/3 hook shank behind the eye. Wrap tinsel in open turns, tie off at front of abdomen; trim waste. Tie in wing case.
Spin dubbing fur thorax roughly onto thread. Wrap a bulging and shaggy thorax.
Pull the wing case over the thorax and bind it down just behind the hook eye.
Trim the waste ends of the wing case, build a neat head, and whip finish. Pick out fur fibers of the thorax to be quite shaggy.

name: Foam Beetle
recipe: Peacock herl, twisted with a piece of tying thread
Black foam, 2mm (5/64") thick, width equal to hook gap
Brightly colored poly yarn or craft foam

steps.text: Wrap a thread base. Trim an end of the foam strip to a point and tie in at the rear of the hook shank, compressing the foam tightly.
Tie in 3-4 strands of peacock herl bundled with a piece of tying thread. Trim waste herl. Position thread ~1.5 - 2 hook eye diameters behind the eye.
Twist the herl gently with the piece of thread and wrap the body in tight touching turns. Tie off the herl and trim the waste.
Pull the foam strip over the body and tie down tightly at the forward end of the peacock herl, thus creating a narrow "waist".
Attach one strand of black rubber legs to each side at the waist. Trim the four legs to length.
Tie in a small piece of bright poly yarn. Trim to length and whip finish at the waist. Trim the foam to form a prominent head.

name: Pheasant Tail Nymph
recipe: Butt ends of tail fibers, twisted into a rope
Butt ends of leg fibers, pulled over the thorax

steps.text: Wrap a thread base and tie in the tail with 2-3 wraps of thread; do not trim. Tie in wire. Lift tail fibers and bind wire to hook shank. Trim wire waste.
Twist butt ends of tail fibers into a rope. Wrap forward in touching turns to ~1/3 hook shank behind eye. Tie off and trim waste ends.
Counter-wrap the abdomen with wire in uniformly spaced open turns. Tie off and trim waste wire.
Tie in leg fibers, tips extending forward for ~2/3 the length of hook shank. Tie in peacock herl just forward of the abdomen.
Wrap peacock herl to form a pronounced thorax; trim waste ends. Pull butt ends of pheasant barbs over the thorax, tie down, and trim waste ends.
Fold tips of the pheasant barbs rearward, half laying along each side. Bind down the folded legs just behind hook eye and whip finish.
Cover the hook shank with a thread base and tie in the ribbing.
Tie in the hackle immediately forward of the ribbing. The dull side of the hackle will face forward when wrapped.
Tie in the peacock herl immediately forward of the hackle. Wrap the thread forward smoothly to a point behind the hook eye.
Twist the strands of herl together and wrap forward in touching turns. Tie off herl behind the eye and trim the waste ends.
Wrap the hackle forward in an open spiral to just behind the hook eye. Tie off the hackle stem and trim the waste.
Counter-wrap the wire through the hackle, being careful to not bind down hackle barbs. Tie off the wire, trim waste, and whip finish.

name: Adams
recipe: Grizzly hen hackle tips, upright and divided
Mixed grizzly and brown dry fly hackle barbs
One grizzly and one brown rooster feather

steps.text: Wrap a thread base. Align wings, shiny sides touching. Wing length equals hook shank. Bind bare stems to shank, tips forward. Trim waste.
Lift wings to vertical and wrap a tight wedge of thread forward of wings. Divide wings ~30° from vertical (60° total). Secure with figure-8 wraps.
Bind tail fibers to hook shank. Tail length equals hook shank length. Trim butt ends of tail fibers.
Dub a tapered abdomen covering ~60% of hook shank, leaving ~40% bare at the thorax for a hackle collar.
Stack two prepared hackle feathers together. Bind their bare stems to the hook shank just forward of the abdomen. Trim waste ends
Wrap hackles together, shiny sides facing forward. Place ~2-3 wraps behind and ~2-3 forward of the wings. Secure hackle, trim, and whip finish.

name: Elk Hair Caddis
recipe: Dry fly dubbing, color to match natural
Medium ginger rooster, palmered through body
Elk or deer hair, natural light or dark

steps.text: Wrap a thread base to the rear of the hook shank and tie in wire. Return thread to the rear and spin dubbing material thinly onto the thread.
Wrap the spun dubbing to a point 1/4 hook shank length behind the eye. Tie in hackle stem with its shiny side facing the hook eye.
Wrap the hackle in open turns toward the rear, finishing at a point mid-way between the hook point and barb. Maintain pressure on the hackle stem.
Counter-wrap the wire forward through the hackle to bind down the hackle stem. Tie off wire and cut the waste of both hackle and wire.
Clean and stack a bundle of hair. Tie in just forward of the hackle with tips extending to hook bend. Keep all of the hair atop the hook shank.
Gather the butt ends of hair, lift them as a bundle, and whip finish under the bundle. Cut the thread and trim the hair bundle to form a prominent head.

name: Letort Hopper
recipe: Yellow dry fly dubbing or poly yarn
Slip of mottled turkey feather; width ~1/2 of hook gap; tip trimmed to a broad "V"; tied in flat
Deer hair, length to bend of hook

steps.text: Wrap a smooth thread base along the hook shank, leaving ~1/3 of hook shank bare behind the eye.
Spin dubbing onto thread (or use poly yarn) and wrap a body over the rear ~2/3 of the hook shank. Leave ~1/3 of hook shank bare at the front.
Tie in the flat underwing. The length should extend beyond the hook bend.
Clean and stack a bundle of deer hair. Tie in the wing forward of the abdomen, length to hook bend. Keep all materials atop the hook shank.
Clean another bundle of deer hair and spin it around the remaining bare hook shank just behind the eye. The hook shank must be bare for spinning.
Lift the butt ends of spun deer hair and whip finish behind the hook eye. Trim the butt ends of hair to form a prominent head behind eye.

name: Parachute Blue-Winged Olive
recipe: Medium dun rooster, barb size ~1½ times hook gap
Olive dry fly dubbing (e.g. Superfine, beaver, etc.)
Same as abdomen, but a darker color.

steps.text: Tie in a thin piece of poly yarn underneath the hook shank.
Gather the poly yarn vertically above the hook shank and wrap thread ~1 to 1½ hook eye lengths up the post. Trim post to hook shank length.
Strip some hackle barbs from the butt end of hackle and tie the stem vertically against the wing post.
Tie in the tail fibers. Dub a thin abdomen and a slightly thicker thorax. Position the thread adjacent to and just behind the wing post.
Wrap ~5 turns of hackle down the wing post in touching turns, with each wrap placed below the previous one.
Tie down the hackle stem with 2-3 tight wraps against the wing post. Bring thread forward and whip finish behind the hook eye.
